Faint horizontal and vertical straight lines at regular ~220 px spacing are mosaic tile seams. A multi-scale dark-ridge (Sato, sigma 1-3, black_ridges) search restricted to the eroded specimen interior returned NO elongated connected structure at all: the 12 strongest suprathreshold ridge components are all 10-20 px compact blobs (largest: x 47-59 y 455-473; x 172-192 y 492-507), i.e. pores, and several of the rest sit on the edge steps at x~415-425. So this looks like an undamaged (or pre-crack) specimen and essentially 100% of the prediction is false positive, dominated by the off-specimen empty field being painted solid. Priority fix: mask off-specimen / off-frame regions before scoring, which removes ~97% of the red here; the residual 2.4% pore speckle then needs a shape/elongation filter.

audits.real_crack_location: none visible
audits.missed_crack_note: No genuine crack is visible anywhere in the enhanced panel. I looked for one three ways and all three agree. (2) Ridge filtering: Frangi and Meijering (sigma 1-3, dark ridges) restricted to an eroded specimen mask return, in the interior, a largest connected component of only ~20-35 px; every response above the 99.9th percentile clusters at the specimen boundary x~440-500, i.e. on the edge rim and the notch roots. For comparison, a real hairline crack a few px wide would produce a component orders of magnitude longer. (3) Notch roots specifically: I zoomed 5x on the specimen side of each of the four edge wedges, the place a fatigue crack would most likely initiate. The wedges are bright material/deposit lobes protruding into the empty field beyond the boundary, and no faint hairline continues from any wedge root into the metal. Conclusion: this field of view shows an essentially undamaged specimen whose right edge is scalloped by the known non-crack wedge/notch feature. The prediction (6.9% of frame, 284 regions) is therefore ~99% false positive, and it is a false-positive-only failure, not a localisation failure - there is nothing here to hit. Priority for fixing: (a) an off-specimen/background mask would remove 83.5% of the red in one step; (b) suppressing the ~113 px mosaic seam lattice removes another 10%; (c) trimming the outer frame border removes a further 4%. Those three geometric filters alone would take this frame from 6.9% predicted area to under 0.2%.
